purpose: does a session-hierarchy structure exist for the #4211 candidate-expansion arm to walk?

definitions.hierarchy_linked_turn: a turn Point reachable from its Session via (:Session)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Point) — the edge the scoping doc's arm walks
definitions.entity_linked_turn: a turn Point carrying (:Point)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) — entity attachment, NOT the hierarchy
definitions.event_level_attachment: an :Event carries a session_id PROPERTY, so (:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) is a session->entity attachment with NO Session->Object edge; counted separately, never folded into the Session counts

edges_the_arm_could_walk.contains: the hierarchy (Session -> turns) the scoping doc's arm uses
edges_the_arm_could_walk.aboutObject: entity attachment; the edge the #4211 gate names. NOT the hierarchy — a graph can have one and not the other

queries.edges_by_type: MATCH ()-[r]->() RETURN type(r) AS edge, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
queries.aboutObject_by_endpoint: MATCH (s)-[r:aboutObject]->(o) UNWIND labels(s) AS sl RETURN sl AS src_label, labels(o) AS dst_labels, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC

queries.episodic_points_any_kind: MATCH (p:Point) WHERE coalesce(p.is_episodic, false) = true RETURN count(p) AS n
queries.turns_with_aboutObject: MATCH (p:Point)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) WHERE coalesce(p.is_episodic,false)=true AND p.pointKind='event' RETURN count(DISTINCT p) AS n

queries.turns_per_session_contains_max_avg: MATCH (s:Session)-[:CONTAINS]->(p:Point) WITH s, count(DISTINCT p) AS c RETURN max(c) AS max_c, toFloat(sum(c)) / count(s) AS avg_c

queries.objects_with_any_attachment: MATCH (o:Object) WHERE ()-[:aboutObject]->(o) RETURN count(o) AS n
queries.events_with_aboutObject: MATCH (e:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) RETURN count(DISTINCT e) AS n
queries.event_attached_session_ids_distinct: MATCH (e:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(:Object) RETURN count(DISTINCT e.session_id) AS n

instrument.note: CONTAINS targets by kind, MEASURED here: event=24999, session-transcript=12606 (37605 total; 24999 event / 12606 session-transcript). This population is not one writer's output — `tortoise/retrieval.py` records that `session-transcript` is written only by the eval ingest lane, and `tools/ask_spotcheck.py::seed_capture_turn_store` hardcodes `"k": "event"`, so it writes none of them. Neither the seeder nor the eval ingest V1 leg (`tools/longmem_eval/ingest.py`, zero `aboutObject` writes) runs the entity-link pass, and `aboutObject_edges` reads 0 here, so that 0 describes THEIR output. ⛔ It does NOT describe the whole eval lane: its V2 leg (`tools/longmem_eval/ingest_v2.py`) DOES write the edge by its own parity route (#2165/E7-D7, gated on `about_entities`), so a census that reads 0 here also measures the ABSENCE OF v2 EXTRACTION OUTPUT in these graphs. The product's own capture path is what the `writer` arm measures, before and after, on a fresh graph.

not_in_this_receipt.every_graph_has_fewer_turns_than_contain: true here over a non-empty population, so the value stands; the defect was `all([])` returning true over ZERO graphs, which this run did not exercise.
not_in_this_receipt.pair_count_guard: the round-2 multiplicity guard -- `contains_distinct_pairs` / `contains_duplicate_pairs`, re-measured above as 37,605 = 37,605 with 0 duplicates -- was itself NULL-BLIND: the query counted `DISTINCT s.id + '|' + p.id`, and a Point with no `id` property concatenates to null, so `count(DISTINCT null)` is 0. On any graph whose Points carry no id (the fixture-seeder shape this arm measures) the column reads 0 pairs beside a non-zero edge count and the duplicate check reports 0 unconditionally. MEASURED on an embedded fixture (one Session, one pointKind='event' Point with no id, one duplicate CONTAINS): 2 edges -> id-concat 0, `WITH DISTINCT s, p` 1. Fixed to node identity in both copies (the query set and the census arm). This run's own 37,605/37,605 is UNAFFECTED (those Points carry ids), and remains as measured.

not_in_this_receipt.role_evidence.uri_source: published '~/.zshrc:48', which was a STRING LITERAL in the tool: nothing in the run read a shell profile, and the URI that was actually measured came from the option's BUILT-IN default (DEFAULT_LIVE_URI) — not from --live-uri on the command line: instrument.argv is ["--out", ...] only, so the measured value is the constant's, asserted by the source and NOT read from any profile or flag. The provenance claim above is therefore UNSUPPORTED for this receipt. The tool now records what SUPPLIED the URI ('--live-uri', or 'built-in DEFAULT_LIVE_URI ... asserted by the constant and NOT measured'), and a re-run will say so.
not_in_this_receipt.skipped_arms_were_exit_0: this run measured every arm it was asked for, so the defect was not exercised: an arm that SKIPPED (store absent, graph not in the file, no TORTOISE_DB_URI, no capture journal) returned a bare {'skipped': ...}, which main collected as nothing, exited 0 and was allowed to REPLACE the target receipt. Skips are now a top-level `unmeasurable` verdict (exit 2, sibling artifact), and an unknown/empty --arms is refused before anything runs.
not_in_this_receipt.truncated_error_prose: the census truncates `skipped_on_error` to 25 entries; the unmeasurable sentence derived its count from that list, so with 30 raising graphs it would have said '25 of ... raised' beside a field saying 30. The sentence now reads the authoritative `graphs_skipped_on_error`. This run's census carried no error field at all, so nothing to correct here.
not_in_this_receipt.uri_field_shape: arms.live.uri and arms.instrument.uri were the --live-uri STRING verbatim, and the writer wrote uri.rsplit('/', 1)[-1] (on a path-less URI that slice returns the whole authority, i.e. the password). Both read arms now publish the URI with its userinfo STRIPPED and the writer publishes the PARSED graph segment. This run's URI was docker://:@localhost:16379/tortoise — EMPTY userinfo — so no credential was ever in this artifact; a re-run emits it as docker://localhost:16379/tortoise.

round_7_note_correction.why: A round-7 review found that `arms.instrument.note` -- the artifact's endorsed explanation for its headline zero -- asserted an ATTRIBUTION this same artifact refutes.
round_7_note_correction.what_was_wrong: The note named ONE writer (`tools/ask_spotcheck.seed_capture_turn_store`) for the whole 37,605-target population, and the tool's `contains_targets_by_kind` comment said that seeder 'writes a `session-transcript` Point per session'. Both are false for this population: `contains_targets_by_kind` here is event=24999, session-transcript=12606, and `tortoise/retrieval.py` records that `session-transcript` is written ONLY by the eval ingest lane and explicitly NOT by that seeder, which hardcodes `k: event` (tools/ask_spotcheck.py). The 12,606 chunk targets are therefore not the seeder's, and a reader re-deriving this census was sent to the wrong writer.
round_7_note_correction.fix: The note is now DERIVED from `contains_targets_by_kind` by the tool's own `_instrument_note()`, so it can only say what the artifact measured; the two source comments were corrected too. The note was updated in place because it is an ASSERTION about the population, not a measured value -- every number in this artifact is untouched.
round_7_note_correction.what_survives: The conclusion the note supports is unchanged and is independently reproduced by the `writer` arm: the stores this arm censuses are not the product's capture path, and none of their writers runs the entity-link pass, which is why `aboutObject` reads 0 there.

not_in_this_receipt.objects_with_gt1_turn_was_UNFILTERED: arms.<store,writer,live>.counts.objects_with_gt1_turn was computed as `MATCH (p:Point)-[:aboutObject]->(o:Object) WITH o, count(DISTINCT p)` — NO turn discriminator, so it counted any attached Point (an extracted claim Point or the fixture seeder's session-transcript Point) as a turn. The sibling `sessions_with_gt1_*` keys were already split into a turn reading and an any-kind reading; this one was not. The key now applies the shared TURN constant, and a new `objects_with_gt1_point` carries the any-kind reading beside it. The values published here (store 0, writer 1, live 0) are the UNFILTERED reading, and the FILTERED value on this population is NOT derivable from this artifact: the writer arm carries 9 Point->Object edges against 8 turns and 3 `statement` Points in contains_targets_by_kind, so at least one attachment is not a turn, and whether an Object holding >1 attachment holds >1 TURN is not recorded here. A re-run emits both keys.
not_in_this_receipt.zero_graph_census_was_exit_0: arm `instrument` marked itself unmeasurable only when a graph RAISED. An instance with NO graphs has no error to count, so a re-run against an empty/wrong instance published `graphs with a turn store: 0 of 0`, all-zero totals and `every graph turns<=CONTAINS: null` — and exited 0, REPLACING this receipt. This run inspected 60 of 173 graphs, so the defect was not exercised here; the arm now refuses (top-level unmeasurable, exit 2, `<name>.unmeasurable.json` sibling) when it inspects no graph at all.
not_in_this_receipt.exit_2_contract_named_one_location: the docstring said exit 2 ALWAYS leaves its reason in this receipt's top-level `unmeasurable` block; the interpreter guard and the `--arms` refusal exit 2 with NO receipt, reason on stderr. not_in_this_receipt.objects_reaching_gt1_event (MEANING): the Cypher bound no relationship: `MATCH (:Event)-[:aboutObject]->(o:Object) WITH o, count(*) AS c`. This receipt's store-arm 211 is therefore either 'objects reached by >1 Event' or 'objects with >1 Edge', and nothing here distinguishes the two. The query now binds the event and counts it DISTINCT, and `objects_with_gt1_event_edge` (count(r)) publishes the edge reading beside it; a re-run emits both keys, and the store arm's 211 must be re-read as the OBJECT reading only.

The legacy-population verdict rests on `session_signature` (1,537 of 1,538 Sessions carry only {id, created_at, turn_count}), which is what the PR body argues from; the sum is published beside it, not as its evidence. The QUERIES entry now says all of this where a reader of the tool will see it.
